config.title: Build CORS config by environment

intro.title: Build CORS config by environment
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) configuration that adapts based on the environment, such as development or production. You will learn to use environment variables to dynamically set allowed origins, making your Node.js application more secure and flexible. The core programming concept involves conditional logic and configuration management using JavaScript objects. You will work with Node.js, the 'cors' middleware, and environment variables to create a single config file that handles different deployment scenarios.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, CORS configuration by environment is essential for managing security across development, staging, and production environments. For example, an e-commerce platform's dashboard might allow localhost origins during development for frontend-backend testing, while restricting to specific production domains like 'shop.example.com' in live deployment. This pattern prevents unauthorized cross-origin requests in production while enabling seamless development workflows, ensuring APIs remain secure yet accessible to legitimate frontend applications.

objectives: Construct environment-specific CORS configuration objects for development, testing, and production
Configure a Node.js application to load different CORS settings based on the current environment variable
Implement conditional logic to select appropriate CORS origins and headers for each environment
Integrate environment-based CORS middleware into an Express server setup
Manipulate CORS options to allow specific HTTP methods and credentials per environment
Apply security best practices by restricting CORS origins in production while allowing flexibility in development
Initialize a centralized configuration module that exports environment-specific CORS settings

steps.title: Define development CORS configuration
steps.instruction: Create a CORS configuration object named 'devCorsOptions' that allows all origins, methods, and headers for development.
steps.hint: Define a constant object with properties like 'origin', 'methods', and 'allowedHeaders' set to permissive values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'devCorsOptions' object is created with permissive CORS settings suitable for development.
successCriteria: The 'devCorsOptions' object exists and includes properties for origin, methods, and allowedHeaders with permissive values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a configuration object, but it might be missing some required properties or have incorrect values. Check that it includes origin, methods, and allowedHeaders.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CORS configuration object wasn't created correctly. Make sure you define a constant named 'devCorsOptions' with appropriate properties.

steps.title: Define production CORS configuration
steps.instruction: Create a production CORS configuration object that restricts origins to specific domains for production. Name it `productionCorsConfig`.
steps.hint: Define a new object with properties like `origin` set to an array of allowed production domains (e.g., ['https://example.com', 'https://api.example.com']), `methods` set to ['GET', 'POST'], and `credentials` set to true.
steps.expectedOutcome: A `productionCorsConfig` object is created with restrictive CORS settings appropriate for production.
successCriteria: The `productionCorsConfig` object is defined with properties like `origin` (array of allowed domains), `methods`, and `credentials`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the `productionCorsConfig` object includes properties like `origin`, `methods`, and `credentials`.
steps.feedbackWrong: The production CORS configuration is not defined correctly. Ensure you create an object named `productionCorsConfig` with appropriate properties.

steps.title: Create environment-based configuration selector
steps.instruction: Create a function named getCorsConfig that returns the appropriate CORS configuration based on the NODE_ENV value.
steps.hint: Write a function that checks the NODE_ENV environment variable and returns either the development or production CORS configuration object.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named getCorsConfig is created that returns either the development or production CORS configuration object based on the current environment.
successCriteria: The getCorsConfig function is defined, checks process.env.NODE_ENV, and returns the appropriate configuration object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it checks NODE_ENV and returns the correct configuration object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't correctly implemented. Check that it uses process.env.NODE_ENV to determine which configuration to return.

steps.title: Apply CORS middleware to Express app
steps.instruction: Call the app.use() method to apply the CORS middleware with the configuration returned by your getCorsConfig function.
steps.hint: Use app.use(cors(getCorsConfig())) to apply the middleware with the appropriate configuration.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Express app will have CORS middleware applied with the environment-specific configuration.
successCriteria: The app.use() method is called with cors() and getCorsConfig() as arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling app.use() with both cors() and getCorsConfig() as arguments.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CORS middleware hasn't been properly applied. Check that you're using app.use() with the correct arguments.

steps.title: Add basic route for testing
steps.instruction: Add a GET route at the root path '/' that returns a simple JSON response with a message property set to 'CORS configuration is working!' to test CORS behavior.
steps.hint: Use app.get() to define a route handler for GET requests to '/'. Inside the handler, use res.json() to send a JSON response.
steps.expectedOutcome: A GET route is defined at the root path that returns a JSON response with a message property.
successCriteria: The code includes app.get('/') with a handler that calls res.json() with an object containing a message property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using app.get() with the correct path and returning JSON with a message property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test route isn't quite right. Check that you're defining a GET route at '/' and returning JSON with a message property.

steps.title: Start the Express server
steps.instruction: Start the Express server by calling app.listen() on the configured port and log a startup message that includes the port number and environment.
steps.hint: Use app.listen() with the port from process.env.PORT or a default (like 3000). In the callback, log a message such as 'Server running on port X in Y mode' where Y is the current NODE_ENV.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be started and a startup message will be logged to the console.
successCriteria: The app.listen() method is called with the port and a callback that logs a startup message containing the port and environment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server, but the startup message should include both the port and environment (NODE_ENV).
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't started yet. Use app.listen() with a port and a callback that logs a startup message.

steps.title: Test the CORS configuration
steps.instruction: Run the server with NODE_ENV=development and NODE_ENV=production to verify the CORS headers change appropriately.
steps.hint: Use the terminal to start the server with different environment variables and check the response headers.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server runs successfully in both environments, and CORS headers differ between development (more permissive) and production (more restrictive).
successCriteria: Server starts without errors in both environments, and CORS headers are verified to change based on NODE_ENV.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server, but make sure to test both development and production environments.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server didn't start or CORS headers didn't change as expected. Check your configuration function and environment setup.
